verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Dehradun for now; the only lendable names are audited, branded formulation units with clean licences — everything else waits.
title: Dehradun Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Dehradun pharma unit buys API and excipients, runs them through formulation, tableting or packing, and sells finished doses to distributors or contract customers.** Cash comes in on distributor terms, so the money is tied up in raw-material stock and receivables long before it returns. **The value sits in the licence and the brand, not the plant** — a formulation line is replaceable; a manufacturing licence and a customer-approved site are not. Peer rating work shows the working-capital drag is structural: Concord Biotech's working capital intensity ran 77% in FY2018, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 [10].

## What has changed now
**The local signal is negative and it is recent.** Uttarakhand GST collections are -19.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 25.2 pp slower [D], and state electricity demand is +4.7% against India +9.5%, 4.8 pp slower [D]. Nationally, output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D] — credit is running well ahead of production, which is exactly when weak units get refinanced rather than repaid. **On top of that, a counterfeit-medicine factory was busted in Dehradun in July 2026, allegedly packing fake drugs under well-known companies' labels** [1][2]. That is a local enforcement event, not a peer result, and it will tighten FSDA scrutiny of every small unit in the district.

## Where the growth is — and who to avoid
**Peer results are strong and they are all in APIs and CDMO, not in local formulation trading.** Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6]; RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth and another acquisition within 12 months [5]. **Pursue the Dehradun borrower who supplies into that chain** — a licensed unit with a named contract-manufacturing or CDMO customer, audited accounts, and a plant the customer has inspected. **Avoid traders, loan-licence operators and any unit whose labels are not its own**; the July raid [1][2] shows how quickly that becomes a criminal matter, not a credit matter.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Rating evidence shows fund-based utilisation swinging from 70-90% to 40-50% in a single quarter at Cohance Lifesciences [9] — so size the limit to the peak, and take monthly stock-and-receivables statements plus GST returns every month. **Take the licence copy, the FSDA inspection report and the customer's site-approval letter at sanction**, and re-take the licence annually. Where the borrower is small — one rated peer ran revenues of Rs. 61.0 crore in FY2024 with high customer concentration [8] — cap exposure to a single customer's share of sales; collect from customer the actual top-three customer percentages.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the licence and the label first.** Any FSDA notice, any label or packaging discrepancy, any change in the named manufacturer on the carton is a stop-and-explain event, not a monitoring item. **Then watch the cash:** receivables stretching past the peer range [10], inventory building while sales fall, or utilisation pinned at the top of the limit [9]. **And watch the state:** another quarter of Uttarakhand GST below India [D] means the local distributor chain is shrinking, so shorten tenor on new limits rather than raising them.
watch: GST turnover falls below reported sales for two months -> freeze fresh disbursement and ask for the sales register
Receivable days move beyond the 48% working-capital-intensity benchmark [10] -> reprice or cut the limit
Any notice, raid or label discrepancy [1][2] -> stop disbursement and refer to legal
Utilisation stays above 90% for two months [9] -> treat as a term-loan request in disguise and decline
State collections stay below India for another quarter [D] -> shorten tenor on all new limits
